comment: Plain-English headlines + summaries per motion, generated by `python -m ingest.summarize_motions` and merged into docs/data*.json by build_dataset. Keyed by a content hash of the motion (see summarize_motions.motion_key) — NOT by motion id, which renumbers. Safe to hand-edit: a corrected entry is never overwritten unless you pass --force.

00b417297504cd46.headline: Two sets of old minutes approved
00b417297504cd46.summary: The agency board approved its minutes from May 15, 2018 and March 5, 2019.
00b417297504cd46.impact: Close to a year of unapproved records was cleared in one go. It touches the file cabinet and no household.

03b50c0af1953d5b.headline: Fire tax deal for Triple Tail area redone
03b50c0af1953d5b.summary: The agency updated its agreement with Unified Fire Service Area on how property tax growth from the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Area is collected and passed along.
03b50c0af1953d5b.impact: Nothing changes for your fire service or your tax bill. This one sorts out how two agencies move money between themselves inside a development area near Triple Tail.

0b6b814e84a30ec1.headline: Mayor Westmoreland named agency chair
0b6b814e84a30ec1.summary: The board named Tom Westmoreland chair of the redevelopment agency, the seat the mayor holds by default under agency bylaws adopted in 2008.
0b6b814e84a30ec1.impact: Chairing the agency lets the mayor speak for the city on economic development. Residents feel none of it.

0cdfefc63d7b5d0c.headline: Water district signs on to Pole Canyon increment
0cdfefc63d7b5d0c.summary: The agency signed a matching agreement with the Central Utah Water Conservancy District covering collection and remittance of property tax growth inside the Pole Canyon project area.
0cdfefc63d7b5d0c.impact: Your water bill is not part of this arrangement. What the district signed governs how the tax growth from the Pole Canyon land is handed back for use in the project.

1133d8f5be873370.headline: Draft 2019-20 agency budget and May 21 hearing
1133d8f5be873370.summary: The agency board adopted a tentative budget for the 2019-2020 year and set a May 21, 2019 public hearing before the final budget is adopted.
1133d8f5be873370.impact: Nothing is locked in at this stage. If you wanted a say on the agency's spending, May 21 was the date to speak.

189f3b217009229f.headline: City to pass Triple Tail tax growth to agency
189f3b217009229f.summary: Eagle Mountain City will collect property taxes in the Triple Tail area and send the growth to the agency, under an agreement the agency board approved.
189f3b217009229f.impact: Of the five collection agreements, this is the city's own: it passes its share of that area's tax growth to the agency. Residents elsewhere in Eagle Mountain see no change to bills or services.

1dcc24954f704e3b.headline: May 7 minutes approved
1dcc24954f704e3b.summary: The agency board approved the minutes of its May 7 meeting; a hearing on the 2019-2020 city budget drew no comment and no vote.
1dcc24954f704e3b.impact: Record-keeping for the agency's files, and nothing more. The budget item that night was listening time only, so no money moved and no rate changed.

1dd9de4bb81d99f4.headline: Utah County signs Pole Canyon tax agreement
1dd9de4bb81d99f4.summary: The agency board approved the Utah County version of the Pole Canyon agreement, covering collection and remittance of property tax growth from the project area.
1dd9de4bb81d99f4.impact: County services carry on as before, and no household pays anything new. This is the county's signature on the tax sharing that funds the Pole Canyon project.

20c5a698f7408902.headline: Fire service area to remit Triple Tail taxes
20c5a698f7408902.summary: Unified Fire Service Area will hand the agency the growth in property taxes from the Triple Tail area, under a deal the agency board approved.
20c5a698f7408902.impact: Fire coverage is not touched by this. The fire service area agreed to send its share of the growth in that area's property taxes to the agency for the project.

24392d0bd2b7e57a.headline: Tax deal approved with QTS Eagle Mountain I
24392d0bd2b7e57a.summary: The agency board approved a participation agreement with QTS Eagle Mountain I, LLC, for a project inside one of the city's community reinvestment areas.
24392d0bd2b7e57a.impact: No terms or dollar figures were read into the record, so this vote alone does not show what the company gets. The deal binds the agency and that company, not city services or your tax bill.

2747f13e74a5b5d9.headline: June minutes approved
2747f13e74a5b5d9.summary: The agency board approved the written record of its June 20, 2023 meeting.
2747f13e74a5b5d9.impact: Housekeeping for the agency's own files. Nothing here reaches a resident.

27727677947aa52d.headline: Carolyn Love named vice-chair
27727677947aa52d.summary: The agency board appointed Board Member Carolyn Love as vice-chair of the redevelopment agency for the year.
27727677947aa52d.impact: A vice-chair runs the meeting when the chair cannot. The choice stays inside the board and reaches no household.

2eedee07e23678e2.headline: Vote on Triple Tail plan reopened
2eedee07e23678e2.summary: The agency board reopened its own vote on the Triple Tail project area plan so the plan could be taken up again.
2eedee07e23678e2.impact: Procedure only. This is the step the board needed before it could vote on the plan a second time, and nothing about it reaches a resident.

2f5690ea9238fc4a.headline: Sweetwater tax increment routed to the agency
2f5690ea9238fc4a.summary: The agency board signed an agreement with the city setting how property taxes from the Sweetwater Industrial Park reinvestment area are collected and passed to the agency.
2f5690ea9238fc4a.impact: Money already collected in that industrial area moves between two sets of books. Nobody pays a new amount, and nothing on the ground changes because of this vote.

34c5baaa36922598.headline: Sweetwater #4 project area plan amended
34c5baaa36922598.summary: Changes to the official project area plan for the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area won the agency board's approval.
34c5baaa36922598.impact: A project area plan sets the boundaries and purposes of redevelopment in Sweetwater #4. What was altered is not stated in the record, so residents there cannot tell from this motion alone what is different.

3ac47c05d79c742d.headline: Deal to route Triple Tail tax money to the agency
3ac47c05d79c742d.summary: The agency approved an agreement with Eagle Mountain City to collect and pass along the growth in property taxes from the Triple Tail project area.
3ac47c05d79c742d.impact: This sets up the plumbing that moves tax money into the agency's project area account. Your own tax bill is unchanged, and you will not see anything on the ground.

433f12a34c82e599.headline: Triple Tail plan adopted with corrected acreage
433f12a34c82e599.summary: Board members adopted the official plan for the Triple Tail reinvestment area, again replacing the 671.49-acre figure with 1,170.44 acres.
433f12a34c82e599.impact: The board took this vote back later in the same meeting and voted on the plan a second time, so this is not the version that stands.

440a8de78430d913.headline: School district signs Pole Canyon tax agreement
440a8de78430d913.summary: The agency approved an agreement with Alpine School District for collecting and remitting the property tax growth generated inside the Pole Canyon project area.
440a8de78430d913.impact: Classrooms and school budgets keep running on the taxes already collected there. The share of future growth on that land is what this document commits, and it takes years to arrive.

45b2344b6a8ad9e6.headline: Alpine School District deal, result unrecorded
45b2344b6a8ad9e6.summary: A matching agreement with the Alpine School District over Triple Tail's new property taxes came to a vote, but the minutes do not record the outcome.
45b2344b6a8ad9e6.impact: Whether the school district's piece was locked in cannot be told from the record. Either way this is agency financing paperwork: no parent, student or homeowner does anything differently.

46a860997671466d.headline: Study of a Mid-Valley commercial project area begins
46a860997671466d.summary: The agency board designated a survey area for a proposed Mid-Valley commercial project area and ordered a draft plan and budget prepared for it.
46a860997671466d.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This starts the study that would later come back to the agency board with a plan and a budget, and only then could tax money be steered into the area.

4f5da9c3499c4e94.headline: Triple Tail project area plan adopted again
4f5da9c3499c4e94.summary: On a second vote, the agency adopted the official plan for the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area, this time with no acreage change attached.
4f5da9c3499c4e94.impact: This is the version of the plan that stands. Landowners and developers inside the Triple Tail area deal with it; the record says nothing that changes for people living outside it.

50a6d0da1c04f13d.headline: June 2 minutes approved
50a6d0da1c04f13d.summary: Written minutes of the agency board's June 2 meeting were approved as the official record.
50a6d0da1c04f13d.impact: Filing work for the agency's own records. It touches the clerk and nobody else.

53fee11aec1e00f8.headline: Sweetwater industrial park budget set at 67.5%
53fee11aec1e00f8.summary: The agency adopted the budget for the Sweetwater Industrial Park reinvestment area #2, counting 67.5% of the site's real property tax value instead of the 75% first proposed.
53fee11aec1e00f8.impact: Nobody's tax bill moves because of this. The percentage sets how much of the site's future property tax growth the agency puts back into the project rather than passing on to the county, schools, fire and water districts.

54d05171c697ab21.headline: Sweetwater #4 project area budget amended
54d05171c697ab21.summary: The agency board amended the official project area budget for the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area. No figures were stated in the motion.
54d05171c697ab21.impact: Project area budgets govern how much property tax growth inside Sweetwater #4 the agency can spend on that area. The record here does not say what changed, so no dollar effect can be described.

571f310b5ac74f07.headline: September 2 minutes approved
571f310b5ac74f07.summary: The agency board approved the written record of its September 2, 2025 meeting.
571f310b5ac74f07.impact: Filing paperwork, and nothing more. You will not see this one.

59e91e8b560b241c.headline: June 2020 minutes approved
59e91e8b560b241c.summary: The agency board approved the written record of its June 16, 2020 meeting.
59e91e8b560b241c.impact: Signing off on old minutes is bookkeeping for the recorder's office. Nothing in it touches you.

5f758565083911bc.headline: Agency budget adopted for 2020-21
5f758565083911bc.summary: The agency board adopted the redevelopment agency's budget for fiscal year 2020-2021, unchanged from the version presented two weeks earlier.
5f758565083911bc.impact: This sets the spending plan for the agency's redevelopment money, not for city services, and the motion names no dollar figures. Residents will see no change to what they pay or receive.

61155b7649a293fe.headline: June 18 minutes approved
61155b7649a293fe.summary: The agency board approved the written record of its June 18, 2024 meeting.
61155b7649a293fe.impact: Housekeeping that makes the earlier meeting's record official. It touches the clerk's file and nobody else.

6489517a339dfa5d.headline: Meeting adjourned at 10:43 p.m.
6489517a339dfa5d.summary: The agency board ended its June 2 meeting at 10:43 p.m.
6489517a339dfa5d.impact: Nothing here reaches a resident. It is the clock stopping on a meeting whose business was already finished.

67528dad8dc19800.headline: 2018-19 agency budget trued up at year end
67528dad8dc19800.summary: The agency board made a final change to its 2018-2019 budget to reflect higher values in the 2012-1 economic development area and the Parkside project area.
67528dad8dc19800.impact: Bookkeeping that catches the agency's accounts up to values already on the ground in those two project areas. You will not see it anywhere.

690ef70c4eccced9.headline: December minutes signed off
690ef70c4eccced9.summary: The agency board approved the written record of its December 3, 2024 meeting.
690ef70c4eccced9.impact: Housekeeping for the agency's own files. Nothing here reaches a resident.

6ab1c1f876ad293e.headline: Abby Ivory named agency executive director
6ab1c1f876ad293e.summary: Abby Ivory, the city's new economic development director, was appointed executive director of the redevelopment agency by the agency board.
6ab1c1f876ad293e.impact: Ivory now runs the agency's daily work and speaks for it with other taxing entities. Staff shuffle only: your services and bills are untouched.

6b2ff4342723775a.headline: Tax deal with Tyson and Oquirrh Wood Ranch
6b2ff4342723775a.summary: The agency board approved a community reinvestment area participation agreement with Eagle Mountain City, Oquirrh Wood Ranch, Utah County and Tyson Fresh Meats, letting staff make minor wording changes.
6b2ff4342723775a.impact: The agreement binds the agency, the city, Utah County and two companies, but the motion states no dollar figures or term. Nothing on your tax bill changes today, and the city attorney can still adjust the wording before every party signs.

6dcd6f1a07e6720a.headline: Meeting adjourned
6dcd6f1a07e6720a.summary: The agency board closed its January 6 meeting at 8:43 p.m.
6dcd6f1a07e6720a.impact: The gavel coming down is not a decision about anything. Nothing here reaches a resident.

6e7a842c530ffe79.headline: Meeting adjourned at 7:38 p.m.
6e7a842c530ffe79.summary: The agency board closed its May 7 meeting at 7:38 p.m.
6e7a842c530ffe79.impact: Nothing here reaches a resident. It is the timestamp that ends the record.

6f41ff61687424cc.headline: Meeting adjourned
6f41ff61687424cc.summary: The agency board closed its May 21 meeting at 9:34 p.m.
6f41ff61687424cc.impact: Adjournment is the clock stopping, not a decision. Nothing about it reaches a resident.

70160f66074d49b2.headline: Pole Canyon project budget adopted
70160f66074d49b2.summary: The agency adopted the spending plan for the Pole Canyon project area, setting where its tax increment revenue comes from and what it may be spent on.
70160f66074d49b2.impact: This is the money side of the Pole Canyon deal, with a cost-benefit analysis putting the city's benefit at about $3 million. A tenth of the increment is set aside for affordable housing.

7353de4f1c4248a1.headline: August 20 minutes approved
7353de4f1c4248a1.summary: The agency board approved the minutes of its August 20, 2024 meeting.
7353de4f1c4248a1.impact: Housekeeping for the agency's own file. Nobody outside the meeting room feels this one.

76efef737c2c5abf.headline: Meeting adjourned
76efef737c2c5abf.summary: The agency board ended its June 18 meeting at 8:29 p.m.
76efef737c2c5abf.impact: Nothing in this one reaches a resident; it marks the close of the evening's business.

7809959020beee8a.headline: June 18 minutes approved
7809959020beee8a.summary: The agency board approved the minutes of its June 18, 2019 meeting.
7809959020beee8a.impact: Nobody outside the agency's record book feels this one. It makes the written account of the June meeting official.

7ccf19a8981dd0fd.headline: Budget for the Sweetwater #4 project area
7ccf19a8981dd0fd.summary: The board took up the official budget for the Sweetwater #4 project area, and the minutes do not record how the vote finished.
7ccf19a8981dd0fd.impact: Without a recorded result, this one is unfinished business. It covers the money side of the project area, so a later meeting is where the outcome will show up.

8ca13e1ae00b1ccc.headline: Plan adopted for Sweetwater data center area
8ca13e1ae00b1ccc.summary: The agency adopted the project area plan for Sweetwater Industrial Park reinvestment area #2, the framework for an agreement to bring a data center to the city.
8ca13e1ae00b1ccc.impact: Consultants told the board the project will not raise property taxes on other properties. The development agreement still has to go to the City Council, so the deal itself is not settled yet.

909b14231b3a7060.headline: October 21 minutes approved
909b14231b3a7060.summary: The board signed off on the written record of its October 21, 2025 meeting.
909b14231b3a7060.impact: Housekeeping that makes the last meeting's record official. It touches the clerk's office and nobody else.

9740298897570f95.headline: June 17 minutes approved
9740298897570f95.summary: The agency board approved the written record of its June 17, 2025 meeting.
9740298897570f95.impact: A months-old record was made official. This touches the clerk's files and nobody else.

99faba6f2eb804bb.headline: Melissa Clark elected agency vice chair
99faba6f2eb804bb.summary: The agency board elected Board Member Melissa Clark as its vice chairperson.
99faba6f2eb804bb.impact: Filling a presiding-officer seat is internal housekeeping for the board. It touches who runs a meeting when the chair is out, and nothing else.

a334ad4ee4c426f9.headline: Agency budget adopted for 2019-20
a334ad4ee4c426f9.summary: The agency board adopted its budget for the 2019-2020 fiscal year, which staff said was identical to the versions presented earlier.
a334ad4ee4c426f9.impact: This budget spends the redevelopment agency's own tax increment money, not city service dollars. Staff said the figures rest on projections and may be amended as parts of the city grow.

ad2dad01b3b1efd9.headline: Utah County to return Triple Tail tax growth
ad2dad01b3b1efd9.summary: The agency board settled terms with Utah County for collecting property taxes inside the Triple Tail area and returning the increase to the agency.
ad2dad01b3b1efd9.impact: This settles which government keeps the growth in property tax from one development area, and the answer is the agency. Your county rate and county services stay as they are.

b0ca036a10cdda97.headline: Sweetwater Industrial Park plan amended
b0ca036a10cdda97.summary: Alongside the budget, the agency board adopted an amended plan for the Sweetwater Industrial Park project area, the document describing what the agency intends to do there.
b0ca036a10cdda97.impact: Residents living elsewhere in Eagle Mountain will not feel this. Anyone with land or a business in the Sweetwater area should read the amended plan, since it sets what the agency can do there.

b3e0834d6a9f12dd.headline: Tax increment plan for 80 acres at Pole Canyon
b3e0834d6a9f12dd.summary: The agency adopted the official plan for the Pole Canyon project area, 80 acres of industrial-planned land where tax increment can pay for development.
b3e0834d6a9f12dd.impact: The site sits in the Pole Canyon master plan and is aimed at industry, with a food manufacturing business under discussion. A resident who spoke raised traffic and the two roads planned there.

b6b46a2860e7e174.headline: Utah County agrees to Sweetwater #4 tax split
b6b46a2860e7e174.summary: The board signed the county into the arrangement too: property tax growth Utah County collects inside Sweetwater #4 goes to the agency.
b6b46a2860e7e174.impact: Property tax the county collects inside the project area funds work in that area. If you live elsewhere in the city, this one passes you by.

b89d032db7c59615.headline: Triple Tail project area budget adopted
b89d032db7c59615.summary: The agency adopted the spending plan for the Triple Tail reinvestment area, correcting the area's size from 671.49 acres to 1,170.44 acres.
b89d032db7c59615.impact: The corrected figure covers about 499 more acres than the resolution first said. It matters to landowners and builders inside that area; if you live elsewhere in the city, this one passes you by.

bbd10ba035192595.headline: Meeting adjourned at 8:44 p.m.
bbd10ba035192595.summary: The agency board closed its June 16 meeting at 8:44 p.m.
bbd10ba035192595.impact: Nothing here for residents: this is the line in the record marking when the board stopped for the night.

be2067ee1b68c1f3.headline: Sweetwater Industrial Park budget amended
be2067ee1b68c1f3.summary: The agency board adopted an amended budget for its Sweetwater Industrial Park project area, the account that governs how property tax growth there is spent.
be2067ee1b68c1f3.impact: No figures were read into the motion, so the size of the change is not on the record. The land is industrial, not housing: businesses and developers building there are the ones affected.

c32fb70d2234dc91.headline: Water district signs Triple Tail tax deal
c32fb70d2234dc91.summary: The agency board signed a collection deal with the Central Utah Water Conservancy District, which will pass the growth in Triple Tail property taxes to the agency.
c32fb70d2234dc91.impact: Nothing on your water district bill changes. The agreement routes that district's share of new property tax from Triple Tail to the agency, which is how a project area gets paid for.

c9221d0491735238.headline: Fire district joins Pole Canyon tax deal
c9221d0491735238.summary: The agency board signed an agreement with the Unified Fire Service Area to collect and pass on property tax growth from the Pole Canyon project area.
c9221d0491735238.impact: Fire coverage where you live is not altered by this. The agreement sets the route by which the fire district's share of new Pole Canyon tax revenue reaches the agency.

c929089b7215b112.headline: Water district to route Sweetwater #4 tax growth
c929089b7215b112.summary: Central Utah Water Conservancy District will hand its share of that same property tax growth to the agency, an agreement the board put in place.
c929089b7215b112.impact: Each taxing entity has to sign separately before the agency can use the money, and this is one of those signatures. You will not notice it anywhere.

d1febc9d22b9963d.headline: City signs its own Pole Canyon tax agreement
d1febc9d22b9963d.summary: The agency and Eagle Mountain City agreed on how the city will collect and remit the property tax growth from land inside the Pole Canyon project area.
d1febc9d22b9963d.impact: Both sides of this deal are the same five people, sitting once as the council and once as the agency board. Your city tax bill is untouched; the city's share of new Pole Canyon revenue is what moves.

d4e57b9961c4cc34.headline: City sends its Sweetwater #4 tax growth to agency
d4e57b9961c4cc34.summary: Eagle Mountain City itself will send its property tax growth from the Sweetwater #4 area to the agency, in an agreement the board approved.
d4e57b9961c4cc34.impact: The city and the agency are separate legal entities, so the city has to sign to hand over its own increment. Homeowners see nothing different on a bill.

d73498ce2d1965a5.headline: Triple Tail project deal with UTLCO approved
d73498ce2d1965a5.summary: The agency board approved its participation agreement with UTLCO Eagle Mtn. Two, LLC, setting the company's terms inside the Triple Tail reinvestment project area.
d73498ce2d1965a5.impact: The record gives no dollar figure and no timeline, so what the company receives is not stated. Nothing here changes your tax bill; it governs how future tax growth from that one area gets used.

d8e6a21da0cfef4d.headline: Study started on Sweetwater Industrial Park tax district
d8e6a21da0cfef4d.summary: The agency board designated a survey area and ordered a draft plan and budget for a proposed Sweetwater Industrial Park reinvestment project area.
d8e6a21da0cfef4d.impact: Nothing is set yet: this only starts the study of whether to route future tax growth from that industrial land back into the site. The board votes on the actual plan and budget later.

d9f3e7a1aa1726a9.headline: Second change to the QTS participation agreement
d9f3e7a1aa1726a9.summary: The agency approved a second amendment to its participation agreement with QTS, a deal between the agency and the company.
d9f3e7a1aa1726a9.impact: The record of this vote does not say what the amendment changes, so a resident reading it cannot tell what the agency and QTS agreed to.

da8d63835ba02a5d.headline: May minutes approved
da8d63835ba02a5d.summary: The agency board approved the minutes of its May 21, 2019 meeting.
da8d63835ba02a5d.impact: With this, the written record of that meeting becomes official. It is a step for the clerk, not for you.

db81c3b839b2db1e.headline: April 21 minutes approved
db81c3b839b2db1e.summary: The agency board signed off on the written record of its April 21, 2020 meeting.
db81c3b839b2db1e.impact: This one touches the recorder's files and nobody else. It makes the April meeting's written account the official version.

f0643c69f8b2659a.headline: December 16 minutes approved
f0643c69f8b2659a.summary: The agency board approved the minutes of its December 16, 2025 meeting.
f0643c69f8b2659a.impact: Signing off on the written record makes December's meeting official. Nobody outside the agency's own files feels this.

f40624f7006880a5.headline: Meeting adjourned
f40624f7006880a5.summary: The agency board ended its March 16 meeting at 7:38 p.m.
f40624f7006880a5.impact: Closing the meeting is the last item on any agenda. There is nothing here for you.

f97d018dae2c7cff.headline: How Sweetwater tax money reaches the agency
f97d018dae2c7cff.summary: The agency board signed off on an updated agreement with the city covering how property tax growth inside the Sweetwater Industrial Park area is collected and handed over.
f97d018dae2c7cff.impact: Your tax bill does not change. This is an accounting arrangement between the agency and the city for money already being collected in an industrial area, and you will not see it.

fc079b4b3248b385.headline: Fire district signs on to Sweetwater #4 tax deal
fc079b4b3248b385.summary: The agency board approved an agreement with the Unified Fire Service Area to collect and pass along property tax growth from the Sweetwater #4 project area.
fc079b4b3248b385.impact: New property tax raised inside that one area goes to the agency rather than to the fire district. No tax rate is set by this, and no bill of yours changes.

fc38704c3f3caf4d.headline: Plan adopted for the Sweetwater #4 project area
fc38704c3f3caf4d.summary: The board adopted the official plan for the Sweetwater #4 community reinvestment project area, the document setting out what the agency intends to do there.
fc38704c3f3caf4d.impact: Adopting a plan builds nothing on its own and asks nothing of you today. It is the agency's statement of intent for that area, and worth reading if you own land nearby.
